scenes.tts: How many motor neurons does a chick embryo's leg column hold at the peak? And how many are left afterwards?
scenes.visual: Title card: Too Many, Then Fewer. A cross-section of the lumbar spinal cord, with the lateral motor column on one side outlined.
scenes.narration: How many motor neurons does a chick embryo's leg column hold at the peak? And how many are left afterwards?

scenes.tts: At the peak, the column that serves its leg holds just over twenty thousand motor neurons.
scenes.caption: At the peak, the column that serves its leg holds just over 20,000 motor neurons.
scenes.visual: Dots fill the lateral motor column, one dot standing for many neurons. A day counter runs to day 6. Label: just over 20,000 at the peak.
scenes.narration: At the peak, the column that serves its leg holds just over 20,000 motor neurons.

scenes.tts: These are Viktor Hamburger's raw counts, from nineteen seventy-five.
scenes.caption: These are Viktor Hamburger's raw counts, from 1975.
scenes.narration: These are Viktor Hamburger's raw counts, from 1975.

scenes.tts: By about day ten of incubation, roughly twelve thousand are left.
scenes.caption: By about day 10 of incubation, roughly 12,000 are left.
scenes.visual: Some dots darken, shrink and are engulfed by a phagocyte shape. The day counter runs to day 10. Label: about 12,000 left.
scenes.narration: By about day 10 of incubation, roughly 12,000 are left.

scenes.tts: Nothing is wrong with this embryo. It has both legs. It will hatch, and it will walk.
scenes.visual: Cut to a schematic chick hatching and walking.
scenes.narration: Nothing is wrong with this embryo. It has both legs. It will hatch, and it will walk.

scenes.tts: So, two questions. How could anyone tell those neurons were made and then died, rather than never made?
scenes.visual: Question card 1: made and then died, or never made?
scenes.narration: So, two questions. How could anyone tell those neurons were made and then died, rather than never made?

scenes.tts: And what decides how many stay?
scenes.visual: Question card 2: what decides how many stay?
scenes.narration: And what decides how many stay?

scenes.tts: This lesson carries one idea. Make too many, then let the target keep what it can support.
scenes.visual: Rule card: Make too many, then let the target keep what it can support.
scenes.narration: This lesson carries one idea. Make too many, then let the target keep what it can support.

scenes.tts: A target is the tissue an axon grows to and connects with. Here, it is the muscles of the leg.
scenes.visual: A leg block on the right with a fixed glow labelled support. Axons from the column grow toward it. Label: target.
scenes.narration: A target is the tissue an axon grows to and connects with. Here, it is the muscles of the leg.

scenes.tts: In the chick limb experiments, changing the target changed how many of the neurons survived.
scenes.visual: Many axons reach the glow. Some connected dots get enough support and stay lit; others get too little and fade. Label: reaching the target does not guarantee survival.
scenes.narration: In the chick limb experiments, changing the target changed how many of the neurons survived.

scenes.tts: It did not detectably change how many were made.
scenes.visual: The number of dots made at the start is unchanged. Tag: chick limb neurons; survival, not production.
scenes.narration: It did not detectably change how many were made.

scenes.tts: More target means fewer deaths, up to a ceiling. No target can rescue a neuron that is not there.
scenes.visual: A dial icon turns a little as the glow grows. A dashed ceiling line labelled all present at the peak.
scenes.narration: More target means fewer deaths, up to a ceiling. No target can rescue a neuron that is not there.

scenes.tts: Some neurons die on a schedule that the target does not set. The lesson ends on them.
scenes.visual: A small clock icon beside a separate group of dots. Tag: not every population.
scenes.narration: Some neurons die on a schedule that the target does not set. The lesson ends on them.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: the embryo makes too many, and in the limb, the target helps set how many survive.
scenes.visual: Closing card: the rule with three tags: survival, not production (chick limb); a dial with a ceiling; not every population.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: the embryo makes too many, and in the limb, the target helps set how many survive.
